"PROJECT: CITY OF CHAOS

A Modern 2D Open-World Crime Sandbox Inspired by GTA 1 @COMMENT_BODY@ GTA 2

You are an experienced indie game development studio consisting of:

- Senior gameplay programmer
- 2D game engine specialist
- Game designer
- AI and NPC systems programmer
- UI/UX designer
- Level designer
- Technical artist
- Sound designer

Your task is to CREATE A FULLY PLAYABLE GAME, not merely describe one.

The game should capture the gameplay philosophy of the original Grand Theft Auto 1 and Grand Theft Auto 2 while introducing modern game design, responsive controls, improved visuals, deeper AI systems and a highly interactive city.

IMPORTANT: This must be an original game. Do not copy GTA assets, characters, logos, maps, music or copyrighted content.

---

1. CORE GAME CONCEPT

Create a 2D top-down open-world crime sandbox.

The player explores a large urban environment, steals vehicles, completes missions, interacts with the city, escapes police, earns money, purchases weapons and gradually becomes a notorious criminal.

The city must feel alive.

The player should be able to ignore missions and simply explore, steal cars, cause chaos, discover locations, fight rival gangs and interact with the environment.

The game must prioritize FUN, RESPONSIVENESS and FREEDOM.

It should feel like a small but polished commercial indie game rather than a technical demo.

2. CAMERA AND VISUAL PRESENTATION

Camera:

- Classic GTA 1 / GTA 2 inspired top-down perspective.
- Slightly angled overhead perspective is acceptable.
- Smooth camera following.
- Camera must never shake excessively.
- Camera should remain centered on the player during movement.
- Smooth transitions when entering vehicles.
- Appropriate zoom level for mobile screens.

Visual direction:

- Retro 2D urban aesthetic.
- Detailed roads, sidewalks, buildings, alleys and parking spaces.
- Distinctive environments and neighborhoods.
- Colorful but atmospheric lighting.
- Day and night cycle.
- Rain and optional weather effects.
- Neon signs, street lights, traffic lights and illuminated windows.
- Animated water and environmental details.

Do not make the city look like an empty grid.

Create recognizable landmarks, interesting streets and memorable locations.

3. WORLD AND CITY DESIGN

Create a compact but detailed open-world city.

The city should contain several distinct districts:

1. Downtown
   
   - Skyscrapers
   - Financial buildings
   - Busy roads
   - Expensive vehicles
   - Corporate security

2. Industrial District
   
   - Warehouses
   - Factories
   - Cargo areas
   - Heavy vehicles
   - Dangerous gangs

3. Residential District
   
   - Houses
   - Apartment buildings
   - Small shops
   - Parking areas
   - Pedestrian activity

4. Commercial District
   
   - Restaurants
   - Stores
   - Gas stations
   - Garages
   - Weapon shops

5. Underground / Criminal District
   
   - Gang territories
   - Secret locations
   - Illegal businesses
   - Mission contacts

Each district must have its own visual identity.

The map must be connected and fully explorable.

Buildings should block movement realistically. Roads must be wide enough for vehicles. Sidewalks must be accessible to pedestrians.

Add alleys, shortcuts, parking spaces and hidden passages.

4. PLAYER CHARACTER

The player character must have:

- Smooth directional movement.
- Walking and running.
- Responsive acceleration and deceleration.
- Collision detection.
- Proper character animation.
- Directional sprite animations.
- Weapon animations.
- Damage animations.
- Death and respawn animations.

The character must NEVER become permanently stuck.

Movement must work reliably in all directions.

The player must be able to:

- Walk
- Run
- Enter vehicles
- Exit vehicles
- Aim
- Shoot
- Interact
- Pick up items
- Take damage
- Die and respawn

5. VEHICLE SYSTEM

Vehicles are one of the most important parts of this game.

Implement a complete vehicle system.

Vehicle categories:

- Compact cars
- Sedans
- Spor (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

(()=>{
const canvas=document.querySelector('#game'),ctx=canvas.getContext('2d');
const W=3200,H=2280,roadsX=[0,620,1280,1940,2600,3200],roadsY=[0,570,1140,1710,2280];
let vw=innerWidth,vh=innerHeight,dpr=1,camera={x:500,y:500},time=0,last=0,started=false,toastTimer=0,weather=0;
const buildings=[],cars=[],peds=[],bullets=[],particles=[],keys={},districts=[
 {name:'DOWNTOWN',bg:'#263b3a',roof:['#435a57','#52635b','#344a49','#626456'],label:'Downtown'},
 {name:'IRONWORKS',bg:'#37403a',roof:['#665649','#75614d','#514d43','#5e584d'],label:'Industrial'},
 {name:'EASTSIDE',bg:'#39443a',roof:['#685449','#77614d','#5a684e','#805d49'],label:'Residential'},
 {name:'MARKET ROW',bg:'#453d35',roof:['#775249','#78654a','#605b48','#8b5a48'],label:'Commercial'},
 {name:'THE CUT',bg:'#342f39',roof:['#554453','#654853','#4a454f','#725347'],label:'Underground'}
];
const player={x:500,y:500,r:12,vx:0,vy:0,angle:0,hp:100,money:250,heat:0,car:null,dead:0,invuln:0,ammo:36};
let mission={active:false,phase:0,from:{x:510,y:430},to:{x:2480,y:1680},reward:500};
const rand=(a,b)=>a+Math.random()*(b-a),pick=a=>a[Math.floor(Math.random()*a.length)],clamp=(v,a,b)=>Math.max(a,Math.min(b,v));
function districtAt(x,y){if(x<750&&y<800)return 0;if(x>1850&&y<800)return 1;if(x<1000&&y>1200)return 2;if(x>1700&&y>1150)return 3;return 4}
function resize(){dpr=Math.min(devicePixelRatio||1,2);vw=innerWidth;vh=innerHeight;canvas.width=vw*dpr;canvas.height=vh*dpr;ctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);document.body.classList.toggle('mobile',vw<850||('ontouchstart'in window))}addEventListener('resize',resize);resize();
function generateCity(){
 // Each block has subdivided lots, service alleys and a recognizable central courtyard.
 for(let gy=0;gy<roadsY.length-1;gy++)for(let gx=0;gx<roadsX.length-1;gx++){
  const left=roadsX[gx]+82,right=roadsX[gx+1]-82,top=roadsY[gy]+82,bottom=roadsY[gy+1]-82;
  if(right-left<140||bottom-top<140)continue;
  const d=districtAt((left+right)/2,(top+bottom)/2),district=districts[d];
  // side streets within selected blocks break up the big avenues
  const alleyX=(gx+gy)%2===0?(left+right)/2:null,alleyY=(gx*2+gy)%3===1?(top+bottom)/2:null;
  const cutsX=alleyX?[left,alleyX-15,alleyX+15,right]:[left,right],cutsY=alleyY?[top,alleyY-15,alleyY+15,bottom]:[top,bottom];
  for(let ix=0;ix<cutsX.length-1;ix++)for(let iy=0;iy<cutsY.length-1;iy++){
   let x=cutsX[ix]+rand(8,16),y=cutsY[iy]+rand(8,16),w=cutsX[ix+1]-cutsX[ix]-rand(22,34),h=cutsY[iy+1]-cutsY[iy]-rand(22,34);
   if(w<55||h<55)continue;
   if(Math.random()<.14){ // pocket park / lot
    buildings.push({x,y,w,h,park:true,d});continue;
   }
   const n=Math.max(1,Math.floor(w/200)),m=Math.max(1,Math.floor(h/180));
   const bw=(w-(n-1)*12)/n,bh=(h-(m-1)*12)/m;
   for(let a=0;a<n;a++)for(let b=0;b<m;b++){
    const bx=x+a*(bw+12),by=y+b*(bh+12),ww=bw-rand(0,8),hh=bh-rand(0,8);
    if(ww<42||hh<42)continue;
    const high=d===0?rand(1,3):d===1?rand(0,1.8):d===4?rand(0,1.5):rand(0,1);
    buildings.push({x:bx,y:by,w:ww,h:hh,d,roof:pick(district.roof),height:high,kind:Math.random()<.18?'shop':Math.random()<.13?'yard':'block',seed:rand(0,1000)});
   }
  }
 }
 // Curated focal landmarks
 buildings.push({x:900,y:140,w:270,h:235,d:0,roof:'#546a61',height:3,kind:'tower',seed:4,name:'NORTHSTAR PLAZA'});
 buildings.push({x:2110,y:890,w:300,h:190,d:1,roof:'#876244',height:0.6,kind:'factory',seed:5,name:'HARBOR FOUNDRY'});
 buildings.push({x:1350,y:1830,w:250,h:210,d:4,roof:'#534052',height:.5,kind:'club',seed:6,name:'THE AFTERHOURS'});
}
generateCity();
const blocked=(x,y,r=8)=>buildings.some(b=>!b.park&&x+r>b.x&&x-r<b.x+b.w&&y+r>b.y&&y-r<b.y+b.h);
function freePoint(){let p;for(let i=0;i<80;i++){p={x:rand(120,W-120),y:rand(120,H-120)};if(!blocked(p.x,p.y,25))return p}return{x:400,y:400}}
const carColors=['#cf654f','#54a3a0','#d3ac56','#7390a0','#8c72a4','#d6d3bd','#63865d'];
for(let i=0;i<40;i++){const p=freePoint();cars.push({x:p.x,y:p.y,angle:rand(0,6.28),color:pick(carColors),type:i%9===0?'van':'car',speed:0,ai:i<18,dir:Math.random()<.5?1:-1,hp:100,stolen:false})}
for(let i=0;i<34;i++){const p=freePoint();peds.push({x:p.x,y:p.y,tx:p.x,ty:p.y,angle:0,speed:rand(18,34),color:pick(['#edc78d','#d17f71','#82aeb0','#a8b67a','#cf9b63']),panic:0})}
function say(text){const el=document.querySelector('#toast');el.textContent=text;el.classList.add('show');toastTimer=2.6}

## Objective
- Build a fully playable original 2D top-down open-world crime sandbox called “City of Chaos,” playable on desktop and mobile.

## Requirements
- Original content; no copied GTA assets, characters, logos, maps, music, or other copyrighted material.
- Include a detailed, explorable city, responsive player movement, vehicles, missions, police heat, combat, and touch controls.
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks and inspect only the latest.

## Decisions
- Implemented the game as a standalone HTML canvas experience with procedurally generated Neon Harbor and custom-drawn visuals.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with canvas rendering, five city districts, player movement/collisions, cars and traffic, pedestrians, vehicle entry/exit, shooting, wanted heat/police, courier missions, pickups, minimap, day/night tint, rain toggle, HUD, and mobile touch controls.
- Confirmed embedded JavaScript passes `node --check`.
- Opened `http://localhost:3002` in Playwright; page title is `City of Chaos — Neon Harbor`.

### Active
- Validate gameplay in-browser, inspect latest screenshot, and fix any runtime/gameplay issues.

### Blocked
- Browser check reported one console error: missing `/favicon.ico` (404), likely non-gameplay.
- No screenshot has yet been captured or inspected.

## Next Move
1. Click “ENTER THE CITY” in Playwright, inspect console, and capture a small JPEG screenshot.
2. Test basic movement, vehicle interaction, and mission start; fix any issues.
3. Consider adding a favicon or suppressing its 404 if desired.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: complete game implementation; currently uncommitted.

## Important Context
- A Python HTTP server was started in the background on port 3002.
- Playwright browser is open at `http://localhost:3002`.

playwright-cli - run playwright mcp commands from terminal

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]
Usage: playwright-cli -s=<session> <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser
  goto <url>                  navigate to a url
  type <text>                 type text into editable element
  click <target> [button]     perform click on a web page
  dblclick <target> [button]  perform double click on a web page
  fill <target> <text>        fill text into editable element
  drag <startTarget> <endTarget> perform drag and drop between two elements
  drop <target>               drop files or data onto an element
  hover <target>              hover over element on page
  select <target> <val>       select an option in a dropdown
  upload <files...>           upload one or multiple files
  check <target>              check a checkbox or radio button
  uncheck <target>            uncheck a checkbox or radio button
  snapshot [target]           capture page snapshot to obtain element ref
  find [text]                 search the page snapshot for text or a regexp, returning matching nodes with surrounding context (like search snippets)
  eval <func> [target]        evaluate javascript expression on page or element
  dialog-accept [prompt]      accept a dialog
  dialog-dismiss              dismiss a dialog
  resize <w> <h>              resize the browser window
  delete-data                 delete session data

Navigation:
  go-back                     go back to the previous page
  go-forward                  go forward to the next page
  reload                      reload the current page

Keyboard:
  press <key>                 press a key on the keyboard, `a`, `arrowleft`
  keydown <key>               press a key down on the keyboard
  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

Mouse:
  mousemove <x> <y>           move mouse to a given position
  mousedown [button]          press mouse down
  mouseup [button]            press mouse up
  mousewheel <dx> <dy>        scroll mouse wheel

Save as:
  screenshot [target]         screenshot of the current page or element
  pdf                         save page as pdf

Tabs:
  tab-list                    list all tabs
  tab-new [url]               create a new tab
  tab-close [index]           close a browser tab
  tab-select <index>          select a browser tab

Storage:
  state-load <filename>       loads browser storage (authentication) state from a file
  state-save [filename]       saves the current storage (authentication) state to a file
  cookie-list                 list all cookies (optionally filtered by domain/path)
  cookie-get <name>           get a specific cookie by name
  cookie-set <name> <value>   set a cookie with optional flags
  cookie-delete <name>        delete a specific cookie
  cookie-clear                clear all cookies
  localstorage-list           list all localstorage key-value pairs
  localstorage-get <key>      get a localstorage item by key
  localstorage-set <key> <value> set a localstorage item
  localstorage-delete <key>   delete a localstorage item
  localstorage-clear          clear all localstorage
  sessionstorage-list         list all sessionstorage key-value pairs
  sessionstorage-get <key>    get a sessionstorage item by key
  sessionstorage-set <key> <value> set a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-delete <key> delete a sessionstorage item
  sessionstorage-clear        clear all sessionstorage

Network:
  requests                    list all network requests since loading the page. each request is numbered for use with the `request` command.
  request <index>             show full details (headers, body, response) of a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-headers <index>     print only the request headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  request-body <index>        print only the request body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-headers <index>    print only the response headers for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command.
  response-body <index>       print the response body for a single network request by its number from the `requests` command. textual bodies are inlined; binary bodies are saved to a file and the path is printed.
  route <pattern>             mock network requests matching a url pattern
  route-list                  list all active network routes
  unroute [pattern]           remove routes matching a pattern (or all routes)
  network-state-set <state>   set the browser network state to online or offline

DevTools:
  console [min-level]         list console messages
  run-code [code]             run playwright code snippet
  recording-start             start recording user actions
  recording-stop              stop recording user actions and print them as playwright code
  tracing-start               start trace recording
  tracing-stop                stop trace recording
  video-start [filename]      start video recording
  video-stop                  stop video recording
  video-chapter <title>       add a chapter marker to the video recording
  video-show-actions          annotate subsequent cli/mcp actions on the page with a callout that names the action and highlights the target element
  video-hide-actions          stop annotating actions performed on the page
  show                        show playwright dashboard
  pause-at <location>         run the test up to a specific location and pause there
  resume                      resume the test execution
  step-over                   step over the next call in the test
  generate-locator <target>   generate a playwright locator for the given element
  highlight [target]          show (or with --hide, remove) a highlight overlay for an element; `--hide` without a target hides all page highlights.

Install:
  install                     initialize workspace
  install-browser [browser]   install browser

Browser sessions:
  list                        list browser sessions
  close-all                   close all browser sessions
  kill-all                    forcefully kill all browser sessions (for stale/zombie processes)

Global options:
  --help [command]            print help
  --json                      output response as JSON
  --raw                       output only the result value, without status and code
  --version                   print version
